records.rationale: Retain Rust Binder priority inheritance for Android libbinder scheduler-policy/minimum-priority/inherit-RT flags, matching the configured optional Rust driver and native Binder semantics. Adapt node decoding to sign-extend the wire priority byte as C Binder does; negative nice values otherwise become large positive values. Clamp unsigned RLIMIT_RTPRIO to the legal maximum before signed conversion, preserving zero-limit fallback and preventing large limits from truncating negative. Preserve CAP_SYS_NICE checks, RLIMIT_NICE bounds, RESET_ON_FORK, process default priority, once-only thread selection, pending/abort restoration and the selected-thread saved priority. Keep the port comparison against the desired priority after RT suppression, matching native Binder; ACK boundary still compares against the original caller priority. Native scheduler implementation is not replaced by these Rust wrappers. Invalid node priorities remain subject to native scheduler validation; no new privilege is granted by an out-of-range value.

records.rationale: Retain saturating subtraction in RT-to-kernel priority conversion. All 256 wire bytes across four policies and additional i32 extremes pass extracted checks. Fair conversion receives a signed byte or bounded task/nice limit on the reviewed paths. No native scheduler validation is removed.

records.rationale: Retain the historical fix to save policy and priority from the actual selected Binder thread, not the receiving process group leader. This prevents persistent wrong scheduling after a transaction; it adds no scheduling privilege.

records.rationale: Retain default-priority restoration before get_work_or_register publishes the waiting thread in the ready list. Reading the entire get_work path shows local/deferred work handling preceding restoration, and registration/interruptible waiting following it. A remote sender can boost a published thread, so a later unconditional restoration could overwrite that boost. No restore remains inside the waiting loop. This ordering is reviewed together with 29293a1515c0; host decision checks do not claim to reproduce scheduler races.

records.rationale: Retain sender-side on_thread_selected before pushing work to a ready target thread under the process state lock. records.rationale: Retain Binder-named trace events and callsites for Android atrace/Perfetto: local atrace explicitly requires transaction, received and allocation events, while Perfetto registers and parses them. Full patch reviewed, including Arc::DATA_OFFSET, runtime layout/accessors, page shrinker snapshots, return/command bounds checks and trace wrappers. Live Rust references protect synchronous pointer reads; page shrinker copies scalar pid/index before releasing locks and does not retain freed range pointers. Adapt diagnostic node_ptr to the user-supplied node address, translated_handle to the translated object, and page-range indices to byte offsets/sizes expected by native Binder tracing. Saturation/reversed-range handling affects diagnostics only. Derive C pointer offsets from their actual Rust containers. Task/transaction metadata is exposed through the existing tracefs access policy, not transaction payload data. Native LTS tracing implementation remains, with driver-selection event removal assessed separately; this decision does not finalize the dual-driver selector.
